description: The Global Food Twin web application is a free, browser-based digital twin of the world's food system. Earth Genome and Better Planet Laboratory at the University of Colorado Boulder built the model, and Development Seed built the interface. Users pick a region or a food category such as grains, pulses, meat and fish or fruit and see where its food comes from and where its production goes, along modelled road, rail, inland waterway and shipping routes. A companion impact analysis tool, available as a Streamlit app, shows how a production shock in one region ripples through to consumers elsewhere, for example a drought or a port closure. Coverage is global, with 3,787 subnational regions in 240 countries, 82 food groups and 2020 as the reference year. The underlying flows and network geometries can be downloaded from Harvard Dataverse under CC BY-SA 4.0. Caveats: flows are modelled with a least-cost routing assumption and exclude air freight; the app itself has no stated licence and no public code repository for the interface; both pages load by script. Simulation uses: exploring exposure of regional food supply to transport and production disruptions before building a detailed model. Related records: the data behind the app are catalogued as data-global-food-twin-food-flows, and WFP HungerMap LIVE (platform-wfp-hungermap-live) monitors food insecurity in near real time.
